newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Swissair loss narrows, sees profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swissair loss narrows, sees profit.

text.p: Swiss flagship carrier Swissair Group, describing 1996 as a transition year for the company, said its net loss narrowed during the first half and that it expected to post a profit for the full year.
The group reported a first half loss of 51 million Swiss francs ($42.71 million) compared to a 86 million franc deficit for the first six months of 1995.
But it also said that measures taken to date should result in a profit this year.

"Nineteen-ninety-six is very much a transition year for Swissair; a number of actions have been taken to help enhance the bottom line, actions which are only now beginning to impact on results," Swissair said in its interim report.
"The Swissair Group expects to post a profit for 1996 as a whole," it added.

Revenues from flight operations were below budgeted expectations as fare levels continued to fall, Swissair said. It also said that net losses for the first half are very much the norm, even in good business years, with the busier travel months of the second half having the biggest influence on annual results.

Most group member companies recorded sizeable improvements in half-year results. But at the group level these increases were largely nullified by the net nagative impact of currency movements and a decline in profits realised on fixed-asset sales, the company also said .
Shares in Swissair rose on the news.
At 0845 GMT Swissair's share were up seven francs, or 0.6 percent to 1,097 francs in a generally weaker market.
"The size of the loss was a positive surprise, we had expected a higher loss. But the forecast is also good," a Swiss dealer said.
The result was in line with analysts' forecast on average, but estimates ranged from a loss of 70 million to a loss of 30 million. ($1=1.1941 Swiss Franc)
